Name: Village Greens Farm Shop at Denbies
Address: Denbies Wine Estate, London Road, Dorking, Surrey RH5 6AA
Description: A proper local larder in the middle of England's largest single-estate vineyard. Known for its British-and-Irish cheese counter, produce from 60+ suppliers within 20 miles and flowers from its own cutting garden. In the 1730s this estate held Jonathan Tyers' notorious Gothic garden on the theme of death, with stone coffins topped by human skulls.
Practical: Mon–Sat 9.30am–5.30pm (5pm Jan–Feb), Sun 10am–5pm. Free Denbies estate parking. Restaurants and takeaway hatch on the estate. Check before visiting.
Nearby: Box Hill Stepping Stones NT car park ~0.7 km; The Stepping Stones pub, Westhumble ~0.8 km
Notes: Website currently shows injected casino spam (appears hacked) – link kept, consider telling the shop. Coords: OSM building (shop=farm).

Name: Village Greens Farm Shop, Ockley
Address: Coles Lane, Ockley, Dorking, Surrey RH5 5LS
Description: The original Village Greens, opened in April 2007 by two office workers who swapped desks for veg crates. Known for its own one-acre field of crops, outdoor trestles of seasonal produce and coffee and cake in the Bee Garden, home to a resident barn owl. Reportedly, Ockley ('oak field') is one candidate for Aclea, where Saxons routed a Viking army in 851.
Practical: Mon–Sat 9am–5.30pm, Sun 11am–4pm (shop's Ockley page; homepage shows a different Sunday time). Takeaway coffee and cakes; seating in the Bee Garden. Check before visiting.
Nearby: The Inn on the Green, Ockley ~1.1 km; St John the Baptist, Capel ~1.7 km
Notes: Same hacked-site caveat as Denbies. Sunday opening conflicts on own site (10am vs 11am). Aclea/Ockley link is a disputed theory – labelled 'reportedly'. Coords: OSM shop=farm.

Name: Kingfisher Farm & Flower Shop
Address: The Watercress Beds, Guildford Road (A25), Abinger Hammer, Dorking, Surrey RH5 6AG
Description: Surrey's last working watercress farm, cutting cress here since 1854. Known for hand-bunched spring-fed watercress, a well-stocked greengrocery and a separate flower shop. In the 1950s Good Friday was so busy the railway added an extra coach just for the cress; the shop itself began in a shed in 1971 because locals kept asking for the odd cauliflower.
Practical: Mon–Sat 9am–5pm, Sun 10am–4pm (flower shop may close Sundays). On-site car park, one-way system. Gomshall station ~0.9 km. Check before visiting.
Nearby: Abinger Roughs NT car park ~1.5 km; The Abinger Hatch pub & St James, Abinger Common ~2.3 km
Notes: Google's own pin for this shop is ~6 km out (near Westcott) – use these OSM building coords, which match postcode RH5 6AG.

Name: Tillingbourne Farm & Smokery
Address: Dorking Road (A25), Abinger Hammer, Dorking, Surrey RH5 6SA
Description: A working farm with its own traditional smokery and trout lakes on the Tillingbourne. Known for home-smoked fish, local venison, Friday fresh fish from the South Coast and catch-your-own trout. It sits in the valley where Abinger Hammer's old hammer-mill once worked iron, the trade that gave the village its name.
Practical: Shop Tue–Sun 10am–5pm; fresh meat Thu–Sun, fresh fish Fri. Trout fishing by booking (Tue–Sun). No pets anywhere on site. Check before visiting.
Nearby: Kingfisher Farm Shop ~0.5 km; Abinger Roughs NT car park ~1.9 km
Notes: Website says it is being rebuilt but all areas operating normally (Nov 2026). Coords: OSM node from FHRS address – near the farm entrance, not verified on the shop building.

Name: Etherley Farm Produce Shop
Address: Etherley Farm, Leith Hill Lane, Ockley, Dorking, Surrey RH5 5PA
Description: A family farm shop at the foot of Leith Hill where almost everything is grown, processed and prepared on the farm. Known for free-range chicken, duck and eggs, seasonal pasture-fed lamb and beef, and its own apple juice, cider and honey. The Keen family have farmed here since the late 1950s and have supplied local Christmas turkeys and geese for over 30 years.
Practical: Winter hours (1 Oct 2026–31 Mar 2027): Tue–Sat 10am–4pm; closed Sun–Mon. Seasonal campsite Apr–Sep. Check before visiting.
Nearby: Etherley Copse NT car park ~0.3 km; The Parrot Inn, Forest Green ~0.6 km; Leith Hill Place ~0.9 km
Notes: Coords: OSM building tagged shop=farm in the farmyard.

Name: Tanhouse Farm Shop & Café
Address: Tanhouse Farm, Rusper Road, Newdigate, Dorking, Surrey RH5 5BX
Description: A farm shop and café in a converted barn, greeted by resident donkeys and with the farm's cattle often in view. Known for homemade pies, pasties and cakes, hearty breakfasts and local produce. A walkers' secret: Tanhouse also cooks the food for the hatch at the top of Leith Hill Tower.
Practical: Open daily 9am–5pm (listing managed by the business). Café with indoor and outdoor seating; parking on site; small play area. Check before visiting.
Nearby: St Peter's Church, Newdigate ~1.2 km; The Six Bells, Newdigate ~1.2 km
Notes: Rechecked Nov 2026: trading (Tripadvisor reviews Jul–Aug 2026; Visit Mole Valley listing). Own domain tanhousefarmshop.co.uk only shows a loading page, so the business's Linktree is used. Leith Hill hatch claim from Visit Mole Valley. Coords: OSM café node; OSM gives postcode RH5 5BE, business uses RH5 5BX.

Name: Denbies Wine Estate
Description: England's largest single-estate vineyard, with 265 of its 380 acres under vine on the chalk slopes below Ranmore. Known for indoor and outdoor tours, cellar tastings, sparkling wine and dining above the vines. The White family planted the first vines in 1986 on land where Prince Albert visited Thomas Cubitt's long-lost mansion in 1851.
Practical: Daily 9am–5.30pm (Jan–Mar weekdays close 5pm); closed 25–26 Dec and 1 Jan. Free parking. Tours and tastings (book ahead), restaurants, hotel. Check before visiting.
Nearby: Box Hill Stepping Stones NT car park ~0.6 km; The Stepping Stones pub ~0.8 km; Westhumble Chapel ruins ~1 km
Notes: Coords: main winery/restaurant building (OSM Gallery restaurant node). Denbies also describes itself as the UK's first certified Net Zero vineyard.

Name: Tanhurst Estate Vineyard & Café
Address: Birketts Farm, Tanhurst Lane, Holmbury St Mary, Dorking, Surrey RH5 6LZ
Description: A young family vineyard on the slopes of Leith Hill, first planted in 2020, with a weekend café in Hither Barn. Known for wine by the glass, cake and bacon baps for walkers and cyclists, and vineyard tours and tastings. Local historian Murray Price believes the lost Battle of Aclea (851), Saxons against Vikings, may have been fought on these very slopes – an unproven theory.
Practical: Café Sat–Sun 10am–4pm. Tastings and tours by booking. Signed from Starveall Corner and NT parking. Check before visiting.
Nearby: Starveall Corner car park ~1.3 km; Leith Hill Place ~1.2 km; Leith Hill Tower ~2 km
Notes: Coords: OSM café node (matches what3words noises.heave.rungs area / Birketts Farm). Dogs: Google tag only, not confirmed – omitted.

Name: Albury Organic Vineyard
Address: Silent Pool, Shere Road, Albury, Guildford, Surrey GU5 9BW
Description: An organic and biodynamic vineyard on the south slopes of the North Downs, planted by Nick Wenman in 2009. Known for award-winning English sparkling wine and rosé, wine-flight tastings and summer vineyard tours. Next door is the Silent Pool, where legend says a woodcutter's daughter drowned fleeing King John and haunts the water at midnight – a tale invented by novelist Martin Tupper in 1858.
Practical: Seasonal: May–Sep Sat–Sun 11am–5pm; shop daily 11am–4pm until Christmas 2026; other times vary, call first. Free parking outside. Tours/tastings bookable. Check before visiting.
Nearby: Silent Pool car park ~0.2 km; Old Saxon Church, Albury ~0.9 km; Drummond Arms, Albury ~1.3 km
Notes: Just outside Mole Valley (Guildford borough), western edge of catchment. Silent Pool legend is labelled as legend; legend originates in Martin Tupper's novel 'Stephan Langton' (1858) per Albury History Society / Guildford Dragon. Coords: OSM shop=farm node.

Name: Silent Pool Distillery
Address: Shere Road, Albury, Guildford, Surrey GU5 9BW
Description: Award-winning gin made in once-derelict farm buildings beside the 'legendary and mystical' Silent Pool. Known for distillery tours, its shop and the Terrace Bar. Founded by a group of friends in 2013, it powers its hand-built German copper still with a restored vintage wood-fired steam boiler.
Practical: See website for shop/bar hours. Tours (18+, book ahead). Shared Silent Pool car park, first hour free; public can't park at the distillery itself. No dogs in buildings. Check before visiting.
Nearby: Silent Pool car park ~0.2 km; Old Saxon Church, Albury ~0.75 km
Notes: Western edge of catchment (Guildford borough). Coords: OSM craft=distillery.

Name: Dorking Brewery & The Tap & Gun
Address: Aldhurst Farm, Temple Lane, Capel, Dorking, Surrey RH5 5HJ
Description: An independent brewery making beer since 2008, now in a converted cattle shed on a working farm. Known for Pilcrow Pale, Saturday brewhouse tours and pints poured a few metres from the tanks. The farm connection runs both ways: the brewery's spent grain goes up the track to feed the cows.
Practical: Tap & Gun: Thu–Fri 10am–11pm, Sat 11am–11pm (site footer shows shorter 'summer' hours). Tours Sat 11.30am, £15, book online. Parking on site. Check before visiting.
Nearby: St John the Baptist, Capel ~1 km; The Crown, Capel ~1 km
Notes: Taproom hours conflict on own site (taproom page vs footer 'Summer Opening Hours' Thu 11–4, Fri 11–7, Sat 11–5). Coords: OSM craft=brewery.

Name: Surrey Hills Brewery
Address: Denbies Wine Estate, London Road, Dorking, Surrey RH5 6AA
Description: A real-ale-only brewery tucked behind the Denbies winery, founded in Shere in 2005 and here since 2011. Known for Shere Drop, once named Supreme Champion Beer of Britain, and Ranmore Ale, bought straight from the brewery. The brewery jokes that its recipes are carved into stone and kept in a vault nearby (they're also on laminated brew sheets).
Practical: Mon–Wed 10am–3pm, Thu–Sat 10am–5pm (brewery shop). Tours and tastings on selected Saturdays. Free Denbies parking. Check before visiting.
Nearby: Box Hill Stepping Stones NT car park ~0.6 km; The Stepping Stones pub ~0.8 km
Notes: Coords: OSM craft=brewery node (Bradley Lane side of Denbies). 'Stone vault' is the brewery's own tongue-in-cheek claim.

Name: Dorking Distillery
Address: Denbies Wine Estate, London Road, Dorking, Surrey RH5 6AA
Description: A small craft gin distillery opened in 2025 inside the Denbies estate, with traditional copper pot stills. Known for guided gin tastings and its Gin Kitchen range, such as Gutsy Monkey and Insane Ostrich. The animal labels are watercolours by Charlotte Godfrey, an artist born and raised in Dorking.
Practical: Mon & Wed–Fri 9.30am–5pm, Sat–Sun 12–3pm, closed Tue. Free Denbies parking. Tasting experiences by booking. Check before visiting.
Nearby: Box Hill Stepping Stones NT car park ~0.6 km; The Stepping Stones pub ~0.8 km
Notes: APPROXIMATE COORDS: not mapped in OSM; reported as next to Surrey Hills Brewery at the back right-hand corner of the main Denbies building, so it shares the brewery's coords – nudge in My Maps if pins overlap. Took over The Gin Kitchen brand (launched 2016).

Name: Dorking Farmers' Market
Address: St Martin's Walk, Church Street, Dorking, Surrey RH4 1UX
Description: A monthly gathering of local growers and makers in the heart of old Dorking, beside St Martin's Church. Known for local meat, veg, bread, cheese and preserves straight from the people who make them. Dorking has long been a market town, and gave its name to the five-toed Dorking chicken, sold at what was once called England's greatest poultry market.
Practical: Third Saturday of the month, 9am–1pm (next dates: 21 Nov, 19 Dec 2026). Town car parks nearby, incl. St Martin's Walk. Check before visiting.
Nearby: St Martin's Church ~60 m; Dorking War Memorial & South Street Caves ~0.35 km
Notes: No official organiser website found; schedule from farmmarkets.co.uk (lists it as running since 2002). Older listings give St Martin's car park, Mill Lane, 9.30–1.30 – verify on the day. Separate council-run traditional Friday market in St Martin's Walk car park, 8.30am–2pm. Coords: centre of St Martin's Walk (OSM).

Name: Food Float
Address: High Street (next to Boots Opticians, 83 High Street), Dorking, Surrey RH4 1AL
Description: Dorking's community-run local food stall, a not-for-profit set up in 2009 after plans for a supermarket megastore. Known for produce from 35+ local suppliers: veg, bread, eggs, meat, cheese, honey and cakes. The name comes from the founders' first plan, to sell local food from a reconditioned milk float; it proved impractical, and the stall first traded in March 2010.
Practical: Fri & Sat 8.30am–2pm, 50 weeks a year. Thursday home deliveries via online shop. Town-centre car parks nearby. Check before visiting.
Nearby: St Martin's Church ~80 m; William Mullins House, West Street ~0.15 km
Notes: Stall location per Food Float site: next to Boots Opticians (outside former Barclays), postcode RH4 1AL. Coords: OSM Boots Opticians node (stall is on the pavement outside). About page gives 2.15pm close; homepage 2pm.
